note: What M1-16 -- probe mode -- costs the window's frame. The window's path gained one usage flag on the HDR target (TRANSFER_SRC, register decision 188), which can in principle cost a GPU its compression of that image, and a constant depth of 0.5 in fullscreen.vert; the processor flags of ADR 0023 also landed in between, and change only CPU code. The 'before' build is M1-15's last commit and the 'after' build M1-16's, instrumented identically with M1-14's timestamp edits, whose anchors match once in both. docs/measurements/m1-16-frame-cost.md describes the tests. The edits are applied in a disposable worktree and never committed. Thirty seconds a run and seven rounds, not M1-15's eight and three: on 2026-09-26 the application ran at about 120 fps, not the 600 to 1,400 of M1-15's day, so eight seconds held fewer frames than the 500 of warm-up and 500 measured the instrumentation needs before it prints; and three rounds could not separate the change from the spread.

edits.why: own the query pool, so it is destroyed before the device
edits.replace:
UniqueAllocator allocator_;
    OwnedHandle<VkQueryPool, VkDevice, vkDestroyQueryPool> measurePool_; // MEASUREMENT ONLY

edits.why: silence the warnings the measurement code would raise
create the query pool and print the device
read the slot's timestamps once its fence has signalled
timestamp at the start of the frame
timestamps either side of the resolve pass
timestamp at the end of the frame
edits.replace:
vkCmdWriteTimestamp2(frame.cmd, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, gMeasurePool, frame.frameIndex * 4 + 3);
    if (auto ok = vkCheck(vkEndCommandBuffer(frame.cmd), "vkEndCommandBuffer"); !ok) return ok;
